label: Bible Study
prompt: Behold, I stand at the _____, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
verse: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
note: Spoken to lukewarm Laodicea — Jesus knocking, waiting for the latch to lift.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that _____ thee.
verse: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee.
note: Just after the bitter waters of Marah turned sweet, God introduces Himself by a new name: the LORD who heals.

label: Sunday School
prompt: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of _____.
verse: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
note: Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt — Jesus later warned simply, 'Remember Lot's wife.'

label: Deep Water
prompt: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that _____, it shall die.
verse: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
note: The exiles blamed their fathers' sins; Ezekiel retired the sour-grapes proverb — each soul answers for itself.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For we are his _____, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
verse: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
note: 'Workmanship' translates the Greek poiema — the root of our word 'poem.' You're God's handiwork.
